doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Visiting American stars as instructors, including Thad Jones and Don Cherry
summary: Visiting musicians at the local club were hired by the school for a day, which made a fantastic education.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well did they have a — who was instructing you?

We had the best instructors, because we took the musicians who came. Like Thad Jones, I even played a lot with Thad Jones even after the education. We had Don Cherry. I mean fantastic musicians. Billy Hart. Horace Parlan, and so on. They came to play at the local jazz club and the school would hire them for a day and they would play with us. It was a fantastic education. Because of course they weren’t teachers at that time.
Well I think you just said we’d play and talk with them. And talking with those people is very informative I find. The lives they led and what it brings to their music.
